title: Oscar and the Orchard Revisited
premise: Astrid Montrose, a pastry chef drowning in café debt, agrees to pose as the partner of Oscar Hale—the estranged heir of the vineyard estate where she once worked summers—at his family's reunion, in exchange for a loan that could save her business. What begins as a transactional charade deepens as Astrid confronts her own history with the Hales, including the inheritance dispute that exiled her from the orchard years ago. As the vineyard's first harvest approaches, Astrid and Oscar must choose between the safe stories they've told themselves and the riskier truth of belonging to each other. The novel ends at the harvest festival, where Astrid forgives herself for walking away, Oscar renounces the inheritance that was never really his dream, and together they reopen the orchard's abandoned cider house—with her café surviving on new terms.
about_author: Mirabel Galloway is the pen name of a former line cook who spent six seasons working vineyard harvests across the Pacific Northwest before turning to fiction. She writes romances about people who mistake self-sufficiency for safety, usually with dessert involved.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Opening in her failing café, Astrid tallies debts, deflects her banker's sympathy, and insists aloud that hearts are trainable muscles. When an eviction notice arrives, she pockets it rather than tell anyone. Emotional beat: brittle denial dressed up as discipline.

chapters.title: The Letter with the Wax Seal
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar receives his grandmother's summons to the Montrose-adjacent Hale family reunion at Thornfield Orchard, along with conditions: come partnered or forfeit his place in the will. He remembers Astrid from their shared harvest summers and finds her café by accident—or so he claims. Emotional beat: reluctant hope.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions of the Heart
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Over cold coffee, they negotiate: one weekend, one fake relationship, one loan that solves everything. Astrid sets rules—no real feelings, no questions about why she left the orchard. Both break a rule before the handshake ends. Emotional beat: wary complicity.

chapters.title: Driving Toward Yesterday
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The drive to Thornfield unspools memories Astrid has buried: the summer she worked the orchard, the falling-out over her mother's contested share of the land, the night she left without saying goodbye. Oscar notices her white knuckles and says nothing. Emotional beat: dread braided with longing.

chapters.title: The Reunion Opens Its Mouth
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The Hale clan descends—sharp-tongued Aunt Vivienne, golden-boy cousin Marcus, grandmother Edith presiding like weather. Introducing Astrid as his partner lands harder than expected when Edith recognizes her. Emotional beat: performance under scrutiny.

chapters.title: Dessert Is a Confession
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Asked to bring a dish, Astrid bakes the orchard's signature apple galette from memory, and the taste cracks the room open—Edith's eyes go wet, Marcus goes hostile. Oscar covers for her beautifully, too beautifully. Emotional beat: the past made edible and undeniable.

chapters.title: Vivienne Knows Everything
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Aunt Vivienne corners Oscar with the truth about Astrid's mother's claim to the orchard—and hints that Edith did something unforgivable to push the Montroses out. Oscar realizes he may have recruited Astrid into the very house that broke her. Emotional beat: guilt arriving early.

chapters.title: Rain on the Trellis
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Trapped together by a storm in the old cider house, Astrid finally tells Oscar why she left: she believed she'd betrayed her mother by loving this place. Oscar admits the inheritance means nothing to him except escape from his father's shadow. Emotional beat: intimacy through honesty.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A near-kiss interrupted by Marcus; both retreat into the fiction they're supposed to be performing. Astrid scolds herself for forgetting the rules; Oscar stops pretending he ever believed them. Emotional beat: want sharpened by interruption.

chapters.title: Edith's Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Edith privately shows Astrid the old account books: her mother's shares were quietly bought out during a crisis, a transaction Edith has regretted for twenty years. She offers restitution—but only if Astrid stays through the harvest. Emotional beat: apology offered as obligation.

chapters.title: Marcus Makes His Move
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Marcus exposes the fake relationship at dinner, framing it as Astrid's scheme to reclaim the orchard. The family turns; Oscar defends her fiercely but too late—Astrid has already heard enough and walks out into the vines. Emotional beat: public rupture.

chapters.title: The Long Road Back
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid returns to her café, ready to lose it with dignity, and finds Oscar waiting on her step—not with the loan money, but with Edith's ledger and an apology that asks nothing. She sends him away anyway. Emotional beat: pride as armor cracking.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Says
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Alone, Astrid rereads her mother's letters and discovers her mother never blamed her for loving the orchard—she blamed herself for selling. Astrid confronts the person in the mirror: the exile was her own choice, made from grief. Emotional beat: the forgiveness the blurb promises begins here.

chapters.title: Oscar Quits the Will
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar tells Edith he wants no inheritance bought with someone else's erasure, shocking the family into silence. Edith, unexpectedly, smiles—it's the first honest thing any heir has said in decades. Emotional beat: liberation disguised as loss.

chapters.title: Harvest Begins Without Them
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Separately, both throw themselves into work—Astrid's café gets a surprise reprieve from a loyal customer's bulk order; Oscar signs on as a hired hand at Thornfield, anonymous among pickers. Each realizes the other is the missing ingredient. Emotional beat: productive heartache.

chapters.title: The Cider House Keys
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Edith visits the café, not to apologize again but to hand Astrid the keys to the derelict cider house and a proposal: restore it, run it, make the Montrose name part of the orchard again. Astrid doesn't answer yet. Emotional beat: belonging offered on new terms.

chapters.title: First Pressing
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The first harvest pressing becomes a small festival; Oscar, flour-dusted and unexpected, shows up at the café with a crate of apples and no speech prepared. He simply asks to help bake. They work side by side until closing. Emotional beat: love as labor, not declaration.

chapters.title: The Galette Test
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid tests a new recipe—her mother's apple, Oscar's grandmother's crust—and names it on the menu for what it is. Marcus arrives, expecting a fight; instead Astrid offers him a seat and the truth about the ledger. Old wounds begin closing. Emotional beat: grace as strategy.

chapters.title: Storm Before the Festival
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On the eve of the harvest festival, a storm threatens the crop and the cider house roof. Astrid and Oscar lead the salvage crew through the night, and in the exhausted dawn, soaked and laughing amid tarps and fallen fruit, they finally kiss. Emotional beat: climax of feeling.

chapters.title: Edith's Toast
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the harvest festival, Edith publicly restores the Montrose share and names the restored cider house after Astrid's mother. Oscar stands beside Astrid not as a fake date but as something neither of them bothers to label anymore. Emotional beat: vindication and tenderness.

chapters.title: The Loan She Didn't Need
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid declines the original loan—her café survives on its own terms now—and instead invests in the cider house partnership. She forgives herself fully at her mother's memorial tree, planting a new graft from the old orchard stock. Emotional beat: self-forgiveness completed.

chapters.title: Orchard Revisited
chapters.summary: Dual POV, closing chapter. One year later: the cider house opens, the café thrives, and Oscar and Astrid host the next reunion on their own terms. The final image is two names carved into the cider house beam, side by side, no longer pretending. Emotional beat: belonging earned, love chosen daily.
